surface_mechanism_description: The surface chemistry deviates from the conventional ligand-exchange scheme, with the formation of a non-volatile acid-base complex between acidic surface sulfhydryl and basic amidine during the H2S half-cycle. The amidine byproduct does not leave the surface, leading to a reduced film growth rate.
evidence: The surface chemistry of this ALD process deviated from the conventional ligand-exchange scheme, as the amidinate surface moiety from Ni(amd)2 was not released during the H2S half-cycle. The formation of a non-volatile acid-base complex on surface between the acidic surface sulfhydryl and the basic amidine was proposed. The mass change in half-cycle was consistent with the proposed scheme and no amidine byproduct was detected in the H2S half-cycle.
